M0 has 10 operators. A model calls them by name with positional arguments; there are no infix operators yet, so `a + b` is written `add(a, b)`. Every operand is `f32` except the ids of `embedding`, its second operand, which are `i32`.

Generated by `modelspec-docs` from the operator registry in [`crates/modelspec-core/src/ops.rs`](https://github.com/beyond10x/modelspec/blob/main/crates/modelspec-core/src/ops.rs): the type checker, the IR builder and the verifier all type an operation through the one function `ops::infer`, and every example below is its answer.

## Summary

| Operator | Tensor IR op | Operands | Example | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [`matmul`](#matmul) | `MatMul` | 2 | `matmul(Tensor<f32, [8, 4]>, Tensor<f32, [4, 1]>)` | `Tensor<f32, [8, 1]>` |
| [`add`](#add) | `Add` | 2 | `add(Tensor<f32, [8, 1]>, Tensor<f32, [8, 1]>)` | `Tensor<f32, [8, 1]>` |
| [`sub`](#sub) | `Sub` | 2 | `sub(Tensor<f32, [8, 1]>, Tensor<f32, [8, 1]>)` | `Tensor<f32, [8, 1]>` |
| [`mul`](#mul) | `Mul` | 2 | `mul(Tensor<f32, [8, 4]>, Tensor<f32, [8, 4]>)` | `Tensor<f32, [8, 4]>` |
| [`relu`](#relu) | `Relu` | 1 | `relu(Tensor<f32, [8, 4]>)` | `Tensor<f32, [8, 4]>` |
| [`transpose`](#transpose) | `Transpose` | 1 | `transpose(Tensor<f32, [8, 4]>)` | `Tensor<f32, [4, 8]>` |
| [`sum`](#sum) | `ReduceSum` | 1 | `sum(Tensor<f32, [8, 4]>)` | `Tensor<f32, []>` |
| [`mean`](#mean) | `ReduceMean` | 1 | `mean(Tensor<f32, [8, 4]>)` | `Tensor<f32, []>` |
| [`mse`](#mse) | `Mse` | 2 | `mse(Tensor<f32, [8, 1]>, Tensor<f32, [8, 1]>)` | `Tensor<f32, []>` |
| [`embedding`](#embedding) | `Embedding` | 2 | `embedding(Tensor<f32, [7, 3]>, Tensor<i32, [10]>)` | `Tensor<f32, [10, 3]>` |

The type checker reports a refused call as a diagnostic: `E-TYPE-012` for a `matmul` contracting dimension, `E-TYPE-003` for operands of different shapes, `E-TYPE-004` for a rank, `E-TYPE-001` for an argument count, `E-TYPE-018` for an operand of the wrong element type ([Diagnostics](diagnostics.md)).

## `matmul`

Tensor IR op `MatMul`, 2 operand(s).

| Call | Result |
|---|---|
| `matmul(Tensor<f32, [8, 4]>, Tensor<f32, [4, 1]>)` | `Tensor<f32, [8, 1]>` |
| `matmul(Tensor<f32, [8, 4]>, Tensor<f32, [3, 1]>)` | refused: `matmul contracting dimension mismatch`: `lhs Tensor<f32, [8, 4]>`, `rhs Tensor<f32, [3, 1]>`, `expected rhs dimension[0] = 4; got 3` |
| `matmul(Tensor<f32, [8]>, Tensor<f32, [8, 1]>)` | refused: `MatMul needs a rank-2 operand; got Tensor<f32, [8]>` |

## Gradients

The reverse-mode rule of each op, for `Y = op(A, B)` and `G = dL/dY`, from the doc comment of `ops::gradient`. `modelspec-runtime`'s gradient tests check every rule against central finite differences.

| op | `dA` | `dB` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Add` | `G` | `G` |
| `Sub` | `G` | `-G` |
| `Mul` | `G * B` | `G * A` |
| `MatMul` | `G @ transpose(B)` | `transpose(A) @ G` |
| `Relu` | `where(A > 0, G, 0)` (`ReluGrad`; 0 at `A = 0`) | |
| `Transpose` | `transpose(G)` | |
| `ReduceSum` | `broadcast_scalar(G, shape(A))` | |
| `ReduceMean` | `broadcast_scalar(G * (1 / numel(A)), shape(A))` | |
| `Mse` | `(A - B) * (G * (2 / numel(A)))` | `-dA` |
| `Embedding` | `embedding_grad(B, G, rows(A))` (`EmbeddingGrad`: row `G[n]` added to row `B[n]`) | none: `B` is `i32` ids |
